rule.bumpSizing: caret-range semantics: crossing the minor field inside 0.x, or any field inside 0.0.x, counts as major
rule.changesetAwareness: a MEASURED pendingRelease sizes the delta against the projected post-`changeset version` version, credited only when it is strictly ahead of declared AND carries a larger bump; not-measured/absent/indeterminate/absent-from-bump-set fall back to the declared version; adequacy is still the same rank comparison (decision 0024)
rule.removedNameRequires: major (values AND type-only names alike — semver-ts.org / Ember RFC 0730)
rule.levelComposition: MAX RANK over the Level-1 subpath-key delta and every per-subpath Level-2 name delta; Level 2 can only raise, never relax (C147)
rule.asymmetricNames: exactly one side carrying a `names` field is INDETERMINATE, never a Level-1 fallback — a pre-Level-2 cache entry must never read as an empty name set (decision 0028 §2.4)
rule.emptyNameSet: an all-asset package is legitimately empty; the v3 marker is the presence of the `names` FIELD, never its contents

THE VECTOR THAT ISOLATES isStrictlyAhead, found by the `creditlaunders` mutant (decision 0028). The other backward case (1.5.0 -> 1.2.0) is rejected by the RANK test alone, so it could not tell the direction guard from the adequacy guard. Here the projection is 0.9.0: `bumpBetween` reads 1.0.0 -> 0.9.0 as a MAJOR because the fields merely differ, and rank(major) > rank(minor), so WITHOUT the direction test a regression-shaped projection would be credited and excuse the removal outright.
The declared version already carries an adequate MAJOR, so the pending changeset adds no headroom and is not credited (creditedVersion null). The rule passes on the declared bump alone.

BACKWARD COMPAT. An absent pendingRelease field must read as not-measured: this is the real web regression (declared 1.1.0, a MINOR) with no pending field at all, and it breaks exactly as under spec version 1.
